audit.why: 52.83% over 547 games. A dashless mage you beat until 6 and lose to after two items — the page and the chart already agree on that shape.
Spike placement is right: your levels 1-3, her level 6 Pop Blossom window, her two-item AP burst. The abilities are also named correctly throughout, which is unusual in this slice.

audit.whatIsWrong: early calls Blooming Burst 'a slow Q', and three strings recommend Aegis Assault as the answer to Tangle-Barbs.
audit.why: Blooming Burst 'blooms again on hitting champions or killing units' — the danger is the second detonation, not the travel speed, and calling it slow tells you to ignore a spell that hits twice. On Tangle-Barbs, Aegis Assault is 'invulnerable to damage from the front' — damage, and frontal only. A root is neither blocked nor prevented by it, so holding the shield against her root spends 22 seconds and still leaves you rooted. Worse, the page misses the rule that decides where you stand: Tangle-Barbs 'becomes larger, faster, and roots for longer' if it passes through a champion, so standing behind an ally makes her root strictly better against you.
audit.corrected: Blooming Burst described by its second bloom, Aegis Assault's role narrowed to her poke damage, and the through-a-champion amplification written in.

audit.whatIsWrong: Inherent Glamour's break condition is never stated, and it is the direct counter to the clone bait the page warns you about twice.
audit.why: Riot: 'Receiving immobilizing crowd control, casting damaging spells, damaging enemy towers as a non-champion' breaks her disguise. Shield Vault is point-and-click immobilising CC — so if you are genuinely unsure which unit is Neeko, the stun itself resolves it, and a disguised Neeko cannot hold the disguise through it. The page tells you to fear the bait and never mentions that your own engage is the reveal.

Tangle-Barbs is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s and is the only thing that lets her chain poke — those twelve seconds are your all-in window. Pop Blossom is 120/105/90s. Shapesplitter is 16s down to 12s, so the clone is not always available either.
audit.corrected: Tangle-Barbs' 12s and Pop Blossom's 120s written into early and mid.

edits.before: Neeko's threat window opens — her R (Pop Blossom) plus E root is a guaranteed pick if you facecheck or get caught after she vanishes via W clone.
edits.after: Neeko's threat window opens — Pop Blossom is 120s and its wind-up is hidden while she is disguised, so the knock-up arrives with no tell at all.

edits.before: Use Aegis Assault (E) to eat her Q poke and Tangle-Barbs root angle, then close with W
edits.after: Face Aegis Assault at Blooming Burst, and never stand behind an ally for the root

edits.before: Land her E root (Tangle-Barbs) to lock you for a full Q + autos poke chain
edits.after: Land Tangle-Barbs through a champion so it roots you for even longer

edits.before: With all three basics you can E her Q, W-stun, and reset Q — but a clean E root from her can flip it, so it's skill-tested.
edits.after: All three basics up you burst her, but Tangle-Barbs roots through Aegis Assault, which only stops frontal damage.

edits.before: Neeko is one of the easiest level 1-3 lanes you get — she has no dash, no stun until 6, and dies to your point-and-click W-stun into a held Comet Spear. Step up at level 1 and bully her off the caster minions; she can only answer with a slow Q (Blooming Burst) and her E root from range. Dodge the Tangle-Barbs root — it's the only thing that lets her chain poke — and if it whiffs, W-vault in and tap-Q for a free trade. By level 3 with all three basics you can E through her Q, stun, and reset Q for a kill.
edits.after: Neeko is one of the easiest level 1-3 lanes you get — no dash, no stun until 6, and she dies to point-and-click Shield Vault into a held Comet Spear. Bully her off the caster minions. Blooming Burst is not slow so much as double: it blooms again on hitting a champion, so the second detonation is the real damage. Dodge Tangle-Barbs — 12s at rank 1, and it is the only thing that chains her poke — and never eat it through a minion line or an ally, because passing through a champion makes it root you for longer.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay yours — empowered-Q poke and your E block keep eating her Blooming Burst for free while she has no kill pressure on you. The lane flips at 6: Pop Blossom (R) plus her E root is a real all-in, and her W clone lets her disguise as a minion or your own champ to bait your W onto a fake. Stop facechecking brush, and don't W-vault blindly into a unit that might be the clone. If you have a lead, take it cross-map with Grand Starfall rather than forcing a 1v1 into her R window.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay yours — empowered Comet Spear and Aegis Assault eat Blooming Burst for free while she has no kill pressure. The lane flips at 6: Pop Blossom is 120s and its wind-up is hidden while she is disguised. On the clone, note what breaks Inherent Glamour — receiving immobilising CC does, and Shield Vault is exactly that, so your own stun is the reveal. Stop facechecking brush regardless. With a lead, take it cross-map with Grand Starfall.

edits.before: Once Neeko hits 2+ AP items she out-scales you hard — a charged R out of fog of war plus E root deletes your squishy frame before your shields matter, and your damage has plateaued. You have no innate sustain to soak her AOE burst. Win this lane in the first ten minutes and convert it with Starfall roams; if it goes long, group with your team and never walk into vision alone, because her whole game is the pick and you're the ideal target.
edits.after: Once Neeko hits 2+ AP items she out-scales you hard — Pop Blossom out of fog into Tangle-Barbs deletes you before Aegis Assault matters, and it only ever covered your front. Your damage has plateaued and you have no sustain to soak the AoE. Win this lane in the first ten minutes and convert with Grand Starfall roams; if it goes long, group and never walk into fog alone, because her whole game is the pick and you are the ideal target.

notes: The ability names on this page were already correct, which is rare in this slice, so the work was mechanics rather than naming. Three corrections. Blooming Burst was called 'a slow Q'; the point of it is that it blooms a second time on hitting a champion, and describing it by travel speed tells the player to shrug off a spell that hits twice. Aegis Assault was recommended three times against Tangle-Barbs; it is invulnerable to DAMAGE from the FRONT, so a root goes through it and the 22 seconds are spent for nothing. And the positioning rule that actually governs her root was absent: Tangle-Barbs 'becomes larger, faster, and roots for longer' after passing through a champion, so standing behind an ally makes it strictly worse for you. Best addition: Inherent Glamour breaks on receiving immobilising crowd control, and Shield Vault is point-and-click immobilising CC — so the clone bait the page warns about twice is answered by your own engage. I deliberately did NOT write the _missing-interactions claim that Tangle-Barbs cancels Aegis Assault, only that the root lands through it; the mel mirror agent declined the equivalent root-cancels-channel claim as unverified and I have kept the two consistent. I also did not write the same file's claim that Inherent Glamour cancels your channel — it is a passive with no CC in it, and the flag has picked up the words describing CC being received.
